title: Generative Adversarial Networks in Time Series: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Brophy, E.; Wang, Z.; She, Q.; Ward, T.
tldr: Systematic review of GAN architectures for time series generation, classifying discrete-variant and continuous-variant GANs and evaluating their applications in data augmentation, imputation, denoising, anomaly detection, and privacy-preserving synthesis.
problem_and_motivation: No comprehensive review existed specifically for GANs applied to time series data generation despite the growing body of research in this niche. Existing GAN surveys focus predominantly on computer vision, leaving time series GANs underexplored.
approach: Conducted a systematic literature review of time series GAN architectures from 2014 to 2021.
Proposed a classification taxonomy splitting time series GANs into discrete-variant and continuous-variant types.
Reviewed architectural evolution including SeqGAN, TimeGAN, SigCWGAN, RCGAN, and other key models.
Evaluated multiple evaluation metrics including MMD, DTW, FID, TSTR/TRTS, and task-specific measures.
Surveyed privacy preservation methods including differential privacy, federated learning, and membership inference attacks.
Compiled popular benchmarking datasets and identified the absence of standardized time series GAN benchmarks.
findings: LSTM-based architectures dominate time series GANs but no single best architecture or loss function has been established across domains.
num: TimeGAN demonstrated improvements over RCGAN, C-RNN-GAN, and WaveGAN on sine wave, stock, and energy datasets.
num: BiGridLSTM-CNN outperformed BiLSTM-GRU, BiLSTM-CNN, and RNN-AE GAN variants on biomedical signal generation.
GANs generate application-specific data and do not generalize well across different time series domains.
No consensus exists on standardized evaluation metrics for time series GANs.
Differential privacy mechanisms can generate data resisting membership inference attacks without severe quality degradation.
GANs effectively augment small and imbalanced datasets for medical, financial, and audio time series applications.

definitions.definition: Generative Adversarial Network, a generative model with competing generator and discriminator neural networks.
Long Short-Term Memory, an RNN variant capable of learning long-term temporal dependencies.
Combines unsupervised GAN training with supervised autoregressive learning for temporal dynamics preservation.
Maximum Mean Discrepancy, a kernel-based two-sample statistical test.
Dynamic Time Warping, an algorithm measuring optimal alignment similarity between time series.
Frechet Inception Distance, a metric measuring distance between generated and real data distributions.
Train on Synthetic Test on Real / Train on Real Test on Synthetic, evaluation paradigms.
Differentially Private GAN, a GAN trained with noise-injected gradients.
Backpropagation Through Time, a training algorithm for recurrent neural networks.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: First comprehensive systematic review specifically targeting GANs applied to time series data generation. Establishes a novel taxonomy classifying time series GANs into discrete-variant and continuous-variant categories.
directly_justifies: No standardized benchmarking dataset exists for time series GAN evaluation.
TimeGAN combines adversarial and supervised training to preserve temporal dynamics.
LSTM-CNN with BCE loss achieved the lowest MMD score of 1.129E-05.
GANs remain application-specific and do not generalize well across domains.
Differential privacy mechanisms can resist membership inference attacks.
limits: Review covers papers up to 2021, missing recent developments.
No standardized benchmarking protocol exists across evaluations.
Experimental comparisons primarily use sine wave and ECG datasets.

limitations: Review period limited to papers up to 2021, excluding recent transformer-based and diffusion-based methods.
No standardized benchmarking protocol exists across time series GAN evaluations.
Experimental comparisons primarily use sine wave and ECG datasets.
Most architectures require fixed sequence lengths, limiting applicability to variable-length real-world data.
GAN training stability issues including mode collapse remain incompletely solved.
Computational cost of some architectures is prohibitive for practical deployment.
